acceptance.given: The three named evaluation-seed records and their provenance fields are present for review.

oracle.expected: Review finds exactly one occurrence of each named seed, with no zero-count or duplicate entries.
forbidden: Any named evaluation seed occurs zero times.
Any named evaluation seed occurs more than once.
oracle.observable: Seed manifest cardinality check reports one occurrence for each named seed.

acceptance.then: The seed review artifact records one-and-only-one occurrence for each named seed.
acceptance.when: Run the FR-6 evaluation-seed cardinality and provenance validation over the current seed records.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Remove one named seed or duplicate one seed record, then run seed cardinality validation; validation must fail.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Enforce exact-once cardinality for all three named evaluation seeds while retaining provenance and non-baseline classification checks.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve the existing seed manifest schema and reject cardinality violations.

slice_hint.state_transition: Seed records move from unspecified occurrence counts to validated exactly-once records.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Validation fails whenever any named seed count is not exactly one; succeeds only when all three counts equal one.

acceptance.given: Pinned inputs and their declared repository identities are available for evaluation.

oracle.expected: A fresh-checkout run reproduces the same coverage result as the pinned-input run.
forbidden: A coverage result that differs from the result produced from the pinned inputs.
oracle.observable: Comparison of pinned-input and fresh-checkout coverage verdicts reports equality.

acceptance.then: The reproducibility report confirms identical coverage results between pinned-input and fresh-checkout evaluations.
acceptance.when: Evaluate pinned inputs in a clean checkout and compare its computed coverage result with the original pinned-input evaluation.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Alter a pinned input or use a non-equivalent fresh checkout, then rerun coverage comparison; mismatch must fail.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Recompute coverage from pinned inputs in a fresh checkout and fail closed on any result divergence.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve replay result categories and mark divergent coverage unsuccessful.

slice_hint.state_transition: Coverage moves from a single-checkout result to a fresh-checkout reproducibility comparison.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Fresh-checkout coverage equals pinned coverage and all bound identities match; otherwise terminal result is unsuccessful.

acceptance.given: A pinned snapshot containing original input identities and historical evidence is available, and historical evidence is immutable.

oracle.expected: Verification reconstructs the original binding identity, confirms historical evidence is unchanged, and a fresh process replay emits evidence bound to that same identity.
forbidden: Fresh replay uses substituted, inferred, or mismatched input identities.
Historical evidence is rewritten during reconstruction.
A replay is claimed without a fresh process execution.
oracle.observable: Replay receipt links reconstructed snapshot identity to a newly executed process receipt with matching target, validator, dependency, and input identities.

acceptance.then: The fresh replay result is attributable to the exact reconstructed pinned identities, with unchanged historical evidence and empty authorization.
acceptance.when: First reconstruct and verify the original binding identity and historical evidence from the pinned snapshot; then launch a fresh process replay using that same identity and reject any identity mismatch.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Substitute or mutate one pinned target, validator, or dependency identity before replay; binding validation must fail.

affected_subjects: SM-6.2 exact identity reconstruction and fresh replay
slice_hint.behavior_change: Implement two-phase replay binding: reconstruct original identities without rewriting historical evidence, then execute a fresh process replay bound to those identities.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Keep historical evidence append-only and preserve receipt identity fields.

slice_hint.state_transition: Snapshot moves from unverified pinned checkout to identity-verified state, then to fresh replay evidence bound to the same identity.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Success requires identity reconstruction equality, unchanged historical bytes, and attributable fresh process execution; mismatch or absent fresh execution fails closed.

acceptance.given: The compiled obligation graph contains Atomic Obligation nodes and command coverage edges.

oracle.expected: Exact-cover validation reports forward and reverse coverage for every Atomic Obligation-to-command relationship with no orphan command nodes.
forbidden: An Atomic Obligation is covered by commands without reverse coverage.
A command node is linked without corresponding Atomic Obligation coverage.
oracle.observable: Exact-cover validator artifact lists complete bidirectional command mappings and zero orphan nodes.

acceptance.then: The graph validation artifact demonstrates mutual exact coverage between each Atomic Obligation and its command nodes.
acceptance.when: Run exact-cover validation during graph compilation and inspect the emitted forward/reverse command mapping artifact.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Delete a reverse command edge or add an orphan command node, then run exact-cover validation; the structural check must fail.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Validate bidirectional Exact Cover for command edges, detecting missing reverse links and orphan command nodes as structural violations.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Retain exact-cover graph schema and fail closed on command-edge asymmetry.

slice_hint.state_transition: Command coverage graph transitions from unverified relation to validated bidirectional exact-cover relation.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Validation succeeds only with complete forward and reverse command coverage and zero orphan nodes; any asymmetry fails.
